title: Interactive incident simulator with realistic timewarp
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need a low-friction, repeatable way for teams to rehearse runbooks and validate incident-bot playbook patches against realistic sequences of telemetry. This PR adds an interactive incident simulator that can replay historical incidents with a 'timewarp' control to accelerate, slow down, or jump between phases, plus a sampled-probe generator to synthesize partial telemetry for noisy or partial-observability scenarios. Key goals: 1) enable non-destructive rehearsals that mirror on-call experience, 2) surface gaps in playbooks (missing assertions, ambiguous steps), 3) provide a lightweight harness for QA and SRE to run deterministic chaos tests. High-level changes: added simulator CLI and web UI, new replay engine with timewarp, sampled-probe telemetry generator, RBAC sandbox flag to ensure no outbound calls during rehearsals, CI integration for deterministic replay tests, documentation and example fixtures. Checklist: - [x] CLI simulator: cmd/sim/main.go and help text - [x] Replay engine: pkg/sim/replay.go (timewarp param, seek, checkpointing) - [x] Web UI: web/ui/simulator.tsx (controls, playback timeline) - [x] Telemetry sampler: scripts/sample-telemetry-generator.py - [x] Sandbox RBAC gating: pkg/auth/sandbox_guard.go - [x] Deterministic fixture sets: fixtures/incidents/* - [x] Unit + integration tests and CI workflow updates - [x] Docs: docs/runbooks/simulator-guide.md and quickstart - [x] Demo workspace templates for SRE-run rehearsals Description of runtime behavior: the simulator accepts a recorded incident trace (supported formats: compact-telemetry-v2, jaeger-compact), validates fixtures, then streams events into the incident-bot pipeline using an isolated subsystem that respects sandbox=true to prevent external side effects. Timewarp supports 0.25x, 0.5x, real-time, 2x, 10x and a 'phase-skip' function that jumps to the next alert group. The sampled-probe generator can emit partial traces to exercise noisy-failure playbooks and can be combined with fault-injection toggles. Commits: [1] 8a3f4b0 - initial simulator skeleton and CLI, basic replay loop, author: mchen [2] 3b9d1ae - add timewarp control, checkpoint/seek, and tests for timing invariants [3] d71b9ce - sampled telemetry generator and fixture authoring tools, add docs [4] f4e2a01 - web UI + playback controls, RBAC sandbox guard and CI workflow Integrations and changed files (high-level): - cmd/sim/main.go (new CLI entrypoint) - pkg/sim/replay.go (replay engine + timewarp) - pkg/sim/fixture_loader.go (compact-telemetry parser) - pkg/auth/sandbox_guard.go (new RBAC gate) - web/ui/simulator.tsx (react control panel + timeline) - scripts/sample-telemetry-generator.py (python generator for fixtures) - fixtures/incidents/* (example incident traces) - docs/runbooks/simulator-guide.md - ci/workflows/sim-replay-tests.yml - tests/integration/sim_replay_test.go - examples/oncall-workspace/demo-sim.yaml Backwards compatibility and safety: sandboxing is opt-in at the workspace level; by default the simulator runs in 'dry-run' mode that only replays into an internal queue. When projects opt into rehearsal-mode they must enable workspace.sandbox=false and a cluster-level allowlist; this is documented in the PR guide. Performance: typical 10-minute incident replay at 10x timewarp completes under 90s on a dev laptop; heavy traces are streamed in chunks to avoid memory pressure. Review summary and conversation: - Arjun Patel (review): "Really valuable tool — please ensure replayed secrets never leave the sandbox and add a KMS-awareness check for archived telemetry." Author reply: "Added sandbox_guard and a verification step that strips or rekeys sensitive spans; documented KMS pattern in simulator-guide.md (see the 'telemetry-handling' section)." - Sofia Martinez (review): "Can we get deterministic seeds for sampled-probe so test runs are reproducible? Also add coverage for simulated partial-observability cases." Author reply: "Added deterministic seeding param --seed and added two deterministic fixture sets in fixtures/incidents/seeded/*. Added integration tests for partial-observability paths." - Liam O'Connor (review): "UI looks good, ~but add keyboard shortcuts to step between phases and a compact timeline export for postmortems." Author reply: "Added left/right keyboard handlers and an 'export-timeline' action on the UI; added docs snippet for postmortem export format." CI and validation: initial CI run reported one flaky integration test (sim_replay_test.go::TestTimingInvariants) failing due to environment time resolution; fixed by adding a mock clock and re-ran. Final CI: unit tests passed, lint passed, integration suite passed on second run, e2e smoke in nightly flagged but not required for merge. Third-party/ops impact: minor new dependency on github.com/ben/timewarp-sim (vendor-checked), small addition to the frontend dependency list (react-timeline-lite). Security review: SRE/security review completed; sandbox guard and telemetry-stripping were requested and implemented. Merge and release notes: merged via squash on 2026-03-02 by Maya Chen (merge commit f8c2d3a). Release notes for customers/internal teams: "Add interactive incident simulator with timewarp for runbook rehearsals and deterministic sampled-probe fixtures; sandboxed by default; see docs/runbooks/simulator-guide.md for usage and safety considerations." How to test locally: run `go build ./cmd/sim && ./sim replay --fixture fixtures/incidents/demo-aws-cpu-2025.compact --timewarp 10 --seed 42` then open the UI at http://localhost:8080/sim to control playback. Related work: ENG-4852 (runbook QA initiative), ENG-4910 (playbook determinism). Future work: integrate scheduler for scheduled rehearsals, record-and-playback for multi-actor rehearsals, and a mode that exports annotated postmortems for learning loops.
